Treatment summary
Patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which the patient's vehicle was struck from the side while
completing a left turn. Presenting complaints included neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent with cervical
whiplash-type injury, and the mechanism described is a plausible cause of these symptoms for a collision of this kind.
Examination documented restricted cervical range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, and imaging findings
clearly confirm the soft tissue injury. The patient's history includes a small strain to the same region several years ago
that resolved completely with no lasting limitation. Care over sixteen visits followed a usual course of manual therapy,
supervised exercise, and home program instruction. Symptoms and function improved steadily, and visit frequency
was tapered as the patient reached a stable point. Billed services reflect the treatment delivered, with no repeated
charges for the same service. At last evaluation the patient reported near-resolution of symptoms and was
discharged to a self-directed home exercise program with return precautions provided.
